extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and applicants/practitioners participating in USPTO patent application interviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, conducting, documenting, and following up on interviews between USPTO examiners and applicants (including WebEx meetings), including agenda content, use of Interview Summary Forms, and required next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a detailed Agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: Having a detailed Agenda can make your interview more productive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful content of a detailed Agenda may include: General intent and/or goal of interview; Brief summary of arguments (if applicable); Applied references; Evidence relied upon; Proposed amendments. Note: Not submitting an agenda alone is not a valid reason to deny the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review the application history before the interview
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing for your interview, review the application history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review prosecution history, prior communications, and prior search/rejections to be prepared to discuss specifics during the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the inventive concept
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing for your interview, understand the inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be able to explain what the invention is and how the claims and specification express the inventive concept so discussion can focus on patentability and claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify allowable subject matter where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing for your interview, identify allowable subject matter where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to point out claim sets or claim elements that are clearly allowable, or to propose claim language that would be allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to explain the position of the previous action
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing for your interview, be prepared to explain the position of the previous action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have clear reasoning for the examiner's rejections or applicant's arguments so the interview can address the basis for the prior action and whether the rejections should be changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a clear plan or agenda for the interview
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing for your interview, develop a clear plan or agenda for the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the specific issues to cover, desired outcomes, and potential amendments or evidence to present during the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the appropriate Interview Summary Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the appropriate Interview Summary Form to document any discussions on the merits of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant Initiated Interview Form 413; Examiner Initiated Interview Form 413B. The appropriate form must be used to create the official record of the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the Interview Summary Form is filled out completely and attachments included
rubrics_metrics.description: When filling out the Interview Summary Form, ensure that the form is filled out completely and attach any agenda or other items (including proposed amendments) provided for the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach agendas, proposed amendments, and any documents relied upon so the file record reflects what was discussed and presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the appropriate time code when documenting the interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the appropriate time code on the Interview Summary Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant Initiated - 112024; Examiner Initiated - 112026. Use the correct code corresponding to who initiated the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document specifics regarding each issue discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summary of Interview should contain specifics regarding each issue discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record sufficient detail so readers of the file can understand what was discussed, including references, claim terms at issue, and factual or legal points raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly identify any agreement reached
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summary of Interview should contain clear identification of any agreement reached between the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly what was agreed, including whether any claims will be allowable, claim interpretations, priority date determinations, application of case law, next steps, or statutory subject matter conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record any agreed claim amendment(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summary of Interview should record any agreed upon claim amendment(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the exact claim language agreed upon and link amendments to issues they resolve (e.g., overcoming specific rejections). Agreement examples include allowability, interpretation of claim limitations, priority dates, application of case law, next steps, statutory subject matter, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer clear, specific substance in interview summaries (avoid vague statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summaries should avoid vague or unclear statements such as 'discussed proposed claim amendments. No agreement was reached.' or 'Agreement was reached because the claims are found patentable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of unclear substance (bad): 'Examiner and practitioner discussed proposed claim amendments. No agreement was reached.'; 'Agreement was reached because the claims are found patentable.' Examples of clear substance (good): Provide factual detail on arguments, citations (e.g., 'See Jones at col. 5, lines 10-20'), state what was agreed or not agreed, identify text to be added to claims, note that an updated search will be conducted, or that certain claims will be allowable pending an updated search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify agreements and record specific issues resolved at interview conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: At the conclusion of the interview, clarify agreements by recording specific issues resolved and noting any interpretations agreed upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify allowable subject matter if any, and ensure the file states what was resolved so follow-up actions are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record specific claim language and specify what prior art is overcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the specific claim language agreed upon and specify which prior art is overcome by those amendments or arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie claim text to the prior art references or rejections overcome to make the resolution concrete in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to specific next steps and assign responsibility with timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to specific steps (examiner and applicant) and assign responsibility for next steps, including setting a completion date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner steps examples: Consult with Subject Matter Expert; Perform Update Search. Applicant steps examples: Consult with Applicant; File Response; Provide Clear Timeline. Set completion date for next step and follow up to ensure actions are taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up and complete administrative actions after the interview
rubrics_metrics.description: After the interview, ensure follow-up actions are completed: enter examiner’s amendment or attorney response into the file and complete the Interview Summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do it; record filings and amendments promptly so the prosecution record remains current and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must initiate WebEx meetings with external users and obtain written authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: WebEx Interview administrative rule: Examiners must initiate all WebEx meetings with external users, and written authorization by applicant is required prior to sending a meeting invite (MPEP 502.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain written authorization from the applicant before scheduling a WebEx; examiners must be the meeting initiator for external WebEx sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: WebEx best practices: minimize visual distractions and disruptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For WebEx interviews, be aware of visual distractions (pets, posters) and eliminate noise and disruptions (silence cell phones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a professional visual background and silence potential noise sources to avoid interfering with the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: WebEx best practices: optimize audio, lighting, camera position, and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: For WebEx interviews, ensure clear audio (place speaker phone close to avoid echoes), proper lighting (avoid dark shadows or harsh glare), place camera at top of monitor, position at comfortable distance, make eye contact, be prepared with materials, and stay engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tips to improve communication: check audio/video before starting, have materials ready to share, look toward the camera while speaking, and remain attentive throughout the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Collaboration Resources Center for tools and instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Patents Collaboration Resource Center for instructional materials on collaboration tools including WebEx, Cisco Phone, and Office Communicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource link: http://ptoweb.uspto.gov/patents/crc/webex.html — consult for help and training on hosting or joining WebEx interviews.
